title: Low blood pressure after intubation for breathlessness
summary: A 31-year-old woman intubated for severe wheeze is hypotensive on the ventilator with a very high CO2.
rationale: Severe expiratory resistance with RR 20 leaves no time to exhale: auto-PEEP builds, venous return falls and SBP drops. Slow rate with high flow, plus bronchodilator, lets the chest empty. Headless engine check on the starting settings and after the named actions: untouched by 2 min: PaCO2 63, pH 7.20, SpO2 99%, Pplat 17, auto-PEEP 9.8, SBP 77; untouched by 60 min: PaCO2 44, pH 7.32, SpO2 99%, Pplat 17, auto-PEEP 9.9, SBP 77; reasonable management by 60 min: PaCO2 67, pH 7.17, SpO2 99%, Pplat 8, auto-PEEP 0.9, SBP 120; typical mistake by 60 min: PaCO2 37, pH 7.38, SpO2 97%, Pplat 34, auto-PEEP 25.0, SBP 37. Values for an arm whose case ended early (improved or deteriorated trigger) are the values when it ended.

retestsMistake.clinicalFocus: Dynamic hyperinflation: fall in venous return from auto-PEEP; fix with lower rate, longer expiratory time, bronchodilator, not by chasing CO2

source: The Ventilator Book 3e (obstructive disease / auto-PEEP chapters, numbers unverified); Marino ICU Book 2025 (severe asthma and COPD exacerbation chapters, numbers unverified); Nunn & Lumb 9e (airway resistance chapter, unverified); GINA severe asthma guidance 2023; Leatherman J. Mechanical ventilation in severe asthma. Chest 2015;147:1671-80. Expiratory resistance 65 cmH2O/L/s and baseline SBP 98 are teaching assumptions (unverified).

changes.vignette: Female 31, 165 cm (PBW 57 kg), 60 kg. VC 480 mL (8.4 mL/kg), RR 20, flow 45 L/min, PEEP 0.

patient.presentingStory: Intubated 40 minutes ago in the ED for status asthmaticus after bag-ventilation. Since arriving in ICU the monitor shows falling blood pressure. She is sedated, ventilator set at 20 per minute "to keep the CO2 down".
patient.history: Asthma since childhood, previous ICU admission. Full escalation.

then.text: Nurse notes: Expiratory hold shows auto-PEEP is high! The systolic pressure is dipping on the monitor.

then.detail: Maintaining or increasing set respiratory rate (>= 20 bpm) in severe bronchospasm leads to dynamic hyperinflation, severe auto-PEEP, and hemodynamic collapse.
Applying high external PEEP (>= 10 cmH2O) in passively ventilated asthma adds directly to alveolar pressure and exacerbates hyperinflation and hypotension.

then.text: Her blood pressure has stabilized on the monitor, peak pressures have come down, and dynamic hyperinflation is resolving.

then.reason: Obstructive strategy applied successfully: dynamic hyperinflation resolved, auto-PEEP lowered, and hemodynamic collapse averted.

then.text: The patient is in severe obstructive shock with unrecordable blood pressure and pulseless electrical activity!

then.reason: Severe dynamic hyperinflation and auto-PEEP caused complete loss of venous return and PEA arrest.

actions.text: You disconnect the ventilator. A prolonged, continuous rush of air escapes from the endotracheal tube over 15 seconds. Blood pressure rises quickly and the heart rate settles; check the monitor.

orderEffects.note: Apnoea trial / ventilator disconnection permits complete exhalation of trapped air
Inhaled beta-2 agonist and anticholinergic reduce bronchospasm
Systemic corticosteroid anti-inflammatory action occurs over hours
Intravascular volume expansion partially counteracts intrathoracic pressure on venous return

predictionPoints.question: You are implementing an obstructive lung strategy (reducing RR to 10-12 bpm and increasing peak inspiratory flow to 70-80 L/min). Over the next 15-30 minutes, which direction will each parameter move?
predictionPoints.explanation: Lengthening expiratory time allows trapped air to escape, reducing auto-PEEP and peak airway pressure. Lower intrathoracic pressure restores venous return and increases SBP. PaCO2 will initially rise due to reduced minute ventilation (permissive hypercapnia), which is well tolerated and protective.

predictionPoints.question: If a mechanically ventilated patient with life-threatening bronchospasm abruptly develops severe hypotension and tachycardia, what is the most immediate life-saving action?
options: Disconnect the patient from the ventilator to allow complete exhalation of trapped air
Increase the set respiratory rate to clear accumulating carbon dioxide
Increase external PEEP to 15 cmH2O to stent open small airways
Infuse 100 mL of 8.4% sodium bicarbonate immediately
predictionPoints.answerKey: Disconnect the patient from the ventilator to allow complete exhalation of trapped air
predictionPoints.explanation: Ventilator disconnection (the 'apnoea trial') immediately vents trapped intra-thoracic air. If hypotension was caused by auto-PEEP and reduced venous return, hemodynamics will dramatically improve within 10-20 seconds.

rubric.description: Reduced set respiratory rate to 14 bpm or below to prolong expiratory time
Obtained an arterial blood gas to assess ventilation and acid-base status

keyPoints: In mechanically ventilated asthma, dynamic hyperinflation and auto-PEEP occur when expiratory time is shorter than the time required for passive lung emptying.
Auto-PEEP transmits to the intrathoracic space, compressing the vena cava and right atrium, drastically reducing venous return and causing severe hypotension or PEA arrest.

The definitive ventilator strategy is obstructive: reduce respiratory rate (10-12 bpm), increase inspiratory flow (70-80 L/min) or shorten Ti to maximize Te, and accept permissive hypercapnia (pH >= 7.15-7.20).
If sudden hemodynamic collapse occurs, immediately disconnect the patient from the ventilator to allow trapped air to decompress.
